A commander’s greatest achievements are measured in the respect he earns for the nation’s people, and your victory at Hai Phong is one that restores the honor of our ancestors who failed where you have now succeeded. With firmly established positions in northern Vietnam and the acquisition of a vital port for supply, the Chinese High Command can advance its plans for the annexation of Southeast Asia with confidence.

A considerable enemy force has assembled at Ulan Ude and is fortifying itself along the approaches to the city. Fortunately, control of the Trans-Siberian Railroad has allowed us to move rapidly into position for an assault on Ulan Ude. You must move quickly before the rebels and their Chinese allies can regroup.

A defeat like the one you suffered at Ulan Ude has dashed our hopes for a swift end to the conflict. With the onset of winter soon near, we will not be able to continue until next year. Your services are no longer needed. Return to headquarters immediately.
A diversion attack took place at Imphal, still to prevent us to restore order in Bangladesh.

A major defeat like the one you suffered at Ulan Ude is the sort of setback which can reverse the tide of war. With your foolhardy maneuvers, you dashed our troops’ hopes for a swift end to the war just when morale was at its highest. Too many soldiers have sacrificed their lives to drive the Chinese army to its knees for you to let them back up. The Joints Chiefs of Staff cannot afford to risk another such defeat and have released you from further duties.

A warrior’s greatest weapon is the fear he instills in his foes. Caught between the threat of an attack on Moscow and our assembly of troops along the Caspian Sea, the Russians have sent large forces in both directions. This has only accomplished the disruption of their defenses. The time is now to begin the second phase of our operation with an assault on Astrakhan. This will secure our positions in Kazakhstan and open the way for the advance on Volgograd. Drive west through Chertonbay and Kalinino to capture Astrakhan and secure a way over the Volga River.

After a long campaign the smokestacks of Volgograd are within sight. The Russian propaganda machine has brought up visions of past glories by declaring the battle for this city the turning point. The Americans and their allies have promised continued support for the failing Russian regime. This is your greatest challenge to date as a multi-national force stands in the way of Chinese destiny. You must seize Volgograd, destroy the UN forces there, and break the Russian will to resist.

After a successful invasion of South Korea, the North Korean attack bogged down around Seoul. The Americans responded by landing at Inchon, hopefully to drive back the North Koreans before the Chinese intervene.

After crossing the Ho Chi Minh trail you must deploy your troops to the north of Khe Sanh.  Clear the hills of any enemy troops and then undertake the attack on the enemy base. Reinforcements from the North with heliport capabilities will arrive to help in the struggle against the enemy positions located in the hills.

After losing Irkutsk, the Russians enlisted the aid of their former state, Kazakhstan, and diverted large numbers of troops and equipment to a staging area near Almaty. This is a desperate attempt to forestall our advance by launching an invasion into China itself. You must crush the Russian build-up as well as capture Almaty and the surrounding towns.
After the People's Republic of China invasion captured Hai Phong, the Vietnamese army launches a counterattack to destroy the Chinese army before it can move on Hanoi.
After the surprise invasion across Lake Baikal, you must press this advantage and seize the city of Irkutsk.
After the war against Russia, China has established a defensive area around Volgograd.

After your victory in Korea we are sending your army to Russia. With the help of our European allies we are planning a push towards Volgograd. However China is anticipating our trust and they are building a large array of fortifications West of the city. Your first mission is to penetrate this layer of fortifications south of the Don river and make possible an attack against Volgograd.

Although the South Koreans desire nothing more than a reunified peninsula, the threat of U.S. forces exerting direct control over them is all that keeps them fighting. In order to alleviate their fears of the U.S. landing an occupation force, it is imperative that you continue the push toward the port of Pusan. Liberate the city of Taejon as swiftly as possible, and sweep away any resistance remaining along the western coast of the peninsula.

An assault on Ekaterinburg, the gateway to the Urals, will begin the offensive. You must capture this key city and nearby Uralmash, and then establish supply points along the towns on the Trans-Siberian Railroad.

As a reward for your past victories Bejing wants to give you the opportunity to become the liberator of Ho Chi Minh. The goal of central command is to make a fast advance on Saigon and continue to surprise the world with our lightning victories over the enemy.  Maybe we can even trap the supporting countries like Japan on the roof of their embassy.

As the capital of South Korea, Seoul is not only a vital military objective, its value as a political asset is immeasurable. The North Koreans occupy what is the most heavily fortified region in the world, while the Chinese have amassed a substantial defensive force in Seoul. You must recapture Seoul and drive the enemy out of the area’s fortifications.

As the capitol of South Korea, Seoul is not only a vital military objective, but also its strategic value as a political asset is immeasurable. You must recapture Seoul and drive the enemy back to gain control of the area’s fortifications.

As the capitol of South Korea, Seoul is not only a vital military objective, its value as a political asset is immeasurable. The North Koreans and their Chinese allies have amassed a substantial offensive force just north of Seoul.  I'm afraid that war is very imminent. You must hold Seoul at all costs if at all possible...  Good luck commander.  You'll need it.

As the capitol of South Korea, Seoul is not only a vital military objective, its value as a political asset is immeasurable. The North Koreans occupy what is the most heavily fortified region in the world, while the Chinese have amassed a substantial defensive force in Seoul. You must recapture Seoul and drive the enemy out of the area’s fortifications.

As the first step we need to break through this line of fortifications and open the way to Volgograd. China is moving forces West to reinforce this line. You must achieve a breakthrough before they reach the front line.

As the primary hub of transport through the Urals and into the depths of Siberia, Kazan is the critical link in all operations against western Russia. You must move quickly to take Kazan and points west.

As the primary means of transport between European and Asian Russia, the Trans-Siberian Railroad is the critical link in all of our operations against the People’s Republic of China. The Chinese are mobilizing additional forces to protect their hold on it. You must move quickly to take Kazan before they cross the Urals. From there, you must capture supply points south along the Trans-Siberian Railroad and secure the waterways down the length of the Volga.

As the primary means of transport through the Urals and into the depths of Russia, the Trans-Siberian Railroad is the critical link in all of our operations against the People’s Republic of China. At Stalingrad, the Russians fought alone while the world watched and hoped for the best.  Now, we are in a great position to help our valiant Russian allies to drive the Chinese out.  The Chinese are weak in Volgograd, but be vigilant.  They are never to be taken lightly.

Chinese High Command views Sakhalin Island in the Sea of Okhotsk as vital to the success of our operations in Russia. You must take the island to secure our eastern flank against Western intervention.
Chinese forces advance along the road to Vladivostok toward Artem and Suchan as U.N. forces are mobilized to aid the weakened Russian troops.
Chinese forces attempt to cut off Moscow by capturing the Volokolamsk highway.

Command of a multi-national force is not to be taken lightly. When lives are lost with no show for it then even the smallest mistakes are magnified well beyond the scope of a strategic disaster. Your handling of the assault on Volgograd has the Russians demanding your head on a platter. It appears Their wishes will be granted.

Commander welcome again to the front. The war with the Hanoi is about to end. As you know, our latest offensives have all ended with an overwhelming victory. The northern part of South Vietnam has been cleared of enemies by the People's Army of China. Hue and Da Nang along other key cities have been also liberated and now it is time for the heart of South Vietnam: Saigon! We need to end this war as soon as possible to prevent any major intervention of USA now that the war in Europe is not going well for Russia.

Comrade commander, we again need your men. As you know, our mid year operations in the province of Kontum have gone well, nevertheless there are still several enemy forward bases that we must destroy. Those bases are too close to our supply routes for Ho the Chi Minh trail and our area 609.  For this reason they must be destroyed. In addition in the province of Kontum an enemy offensive is anticipated and our enemies do not have to count on those outposts.

Coveting it as the cornerstone to their domination of the Asian sphere, the Chinese are pouring everything they have into the defense of Indochina. Our navies have managed to thwart enemy operations in the South China Sea, but victory for our forces on land requires a firm foundation to operate from. You are to establish defensive positions east of the Nang Rang River, then assault Bangkok and secure the rail lines north along the Chayo Praya River to Saraburi.
Crossing Pakistani Border - July 20th, 2012
Dash for Ho Chi Minh City

Ekaterinburg stands as the gateway through the Urals where the Chinese continue to strip Russia of its precious resources. Your victory at Astrakhan has paid off as the Russians were able to field a force from Volgograd in time to join our assault through the mountain pass. The U.S. force is charged with the capture of Ekaterinburg and securing the rail lines running east into Siberia; the Russian force advancing toward Sysert’ from the south is to provide flanking support.
Escape from Vung Tau - December 29th, 2014

Following the conquest of Volgograd Russians are in disaray. Most of the military refuses to fight anymore and the Russian president is on the brink of colapse. Meanwhile, their western allies are sending forces towards Volgograd. The last russian reserves are trying to mount a counter-attack.
From our secure foothold in Bangkok, our forces were able to land without incident and have managed to push the already decimated Chinese back into Laos and Vietnam.

Good morning comrade commander. As you know, our campaign of attacking enemy forward bases continues.  Khe Sanh is the provincial capital and the key towards controlling our national Route 9. Your mission is to coordinate the attack against the Vietnamese base at Khe Sanh. That base is a constant threat against our supply routes through Laos.
Good work comrade. The south Koreans have been defeated and they are not going to be a problem. Anyway it seem they have assumed a defensive role at this time and Tuy Hoa is still well protected.

I had planned a small banquet and a speech in your honor.  I had written down, "The People’s Republic of China got a true taste of modern warfare along the Volga. Your timely recapture of Volgograd and its industries has given the Russian nation and its teetering government a much needed boost."

If ever the U.S. needed a slam-dunk, it was at Ho Chi Minh City, and you delivered it. China has relinquished control of the Spratly Islands, giving our allies access to the oil resources there and leaving the field wide open for our naval forces to dominate in the South China Sea.
In order to secure our conquests in Siberia, you must secure all of the Russian Far East up to Ekaterinburg as a bulwark against future attacks by our enemies.

Intelligence has confirmed that an American force has been sent to help the battered Russians. Despite the presence of the Americans in the vicinity of Irkutsk, you must immediately establish the bridgehead across Lake Baikal, and then seize the city of Irkutsk. This is your opportunity to show the world the power of the Chinese War Machine.

It had been hoped that you would not repeat the defeats of our ancestors at Hai Phong, but your fear of an ancient foe has mastered you. The Premier has ordered your immediate dismissal for the embarrassment that your loss burdens the People’s Republic of China with.

It has been three long months since our declaration of war. In that time we have seen many disasters including Seoul and Taejon. Now you must defend Pusan, much like the Marines did a few decades ago.  If you can save Pusan, then we may be able to land reinforcements from Japan.

It has been three long years since our declaration of war. In that time we have seen many disasters, Irkutsk, Volgograd, and Southeast Asia. Now, after a fierce battle down the Korean Peninsula, we have finally stopped the Chinese and their North Korean allies outside the Korean city of Pusan. You have been selected to strike the blow that will liberate Asia from the Chinese Red Banner.
It is crucial that you capture Taejon and the roads north to Choch’iwan quickly, as well as securing the western coast of the peninsula north to Hongsong.

It is time to settle scores with our age-old enemies, the Vietnamese as well as the transformed puppet states of the West, Thailand and Malaysia. For far too long we have watched as this area break away from tradition and transform into the ways of the decadent West. Your first objective is to seize the Vietnamese capital of Hanoi and capture the port of Hai Phong. Be prepared for bitter resistance, as the Vietnamese are well known for their tenacious defense.

Judging by the thrashing you took at Astrakhan, it is difficult to believe you were in command of the finest military force in the world. Those men deserved better. Your replacement has already been dispatched. Perhaps babysitting the white-coats at McMurdo Station will prove more in line with your abilities. Start packing immediately.

Khabarovsk is an ideal place to unleash the offensive against the Russian regime. By taking this vital city and cutting all communications along the Trans-Siberian Railroad we can isolate the Russian Far East. You must quickly seize Khabarovsk. This will set up our forces to take Sakhalin island and then the port of Vladivostok from its undefended northern front. Speed is the key to your success.

Led by a revamped American military machine that has stopped the Chinese drive at Pusan, the United Nations attempt to halt the People's Republic of China in South Korea, then continue the liberation of all Chinese held foreign territories.

Led by a revamped European military machine that has stopped the Chinese drive at Pusan, the United Nations led by the French, the British and the Germans attempt to halt the People's Republic of China in South Korea, then continue the liberation of all Chinese held foreign territories.

Look around you Commander.  It is hard to believe that here was fought the most significant battle of World War II.  While the name of the city has changed from Tsaritsyn to Stalingrad to Volgograd, the terrain is the same, the people are the same, and little else has changed.  Only the buildings are perhaps more modern than before.  Look at the great sculpture of Mother Russia towering over the city.  Did you know that it is the world's tallest and that it is twice as tall as our own Statue of Liberty?

Our forces have made a surprise invasion near Suchan. Your forces must advance to capture the cities along the Trans-Siberian Railroad, thus securing a flanking position to Vladivostok before the rebels can destroy the port.

Smashing the Chinese defenses at Almaty was an impressive opening to your upcoming Siberian offensive. It gave the newly rebuilt Russian army the confidence it needed. South Korean insurgents revolted against the occupational forces in Taejon, mercilessly driving them from the city. Continuing the attacks, the South Koreans try to push the North Koreans back to the Kum River.

Stretched to the limit of its supply lines, the Chinese armies bog down as they advance on Astrakhan. Hoping to crush the offensive, Russian reinforcements move up as the two forces square off at the Mouths of the Volga.

Thailand has long been held hostage to Western imperialism. Now, your action in Vietnam has their greedy palms sweating as they see their control slipping away. Drive south through Phra Nahka Si Ayutthaya to capture Bangkok and secure the rail lines to the east.

The Chinese High Command needs commanders who are wise enough to see opportunity and bold enough to seize it. Your failure to capture Irkutsk was a show of neither, and you are ordered to relinquish your command.
The Chinese offensive in Siberia continues its steamrolling attacks with an assault on Almaty. The Russians respond by sending what troops they can to aid Kazakhstan in its defense of Almaty.

The People’s Republic of China invasion of Sakhalin Island is a desperate attempt to maintain a foothold in the Russian Far East from which it can intimidate both Russia and Japan. You must expand the landing at Poronask and destroy the enemy resistance on the island.

The Premier has expressed satisfaction in your victory on Sakhalin and has chosen you to lead our forces to the port of Vladivostok. Do not waste away this excellent opportunity to secure the Russian Far East.

The Russian President is outraged at your dismal performance in the defeat at Khabarovsk, stating that only American arrogance would demand entrusting the liberation of his country to a foreign commander. The Russian attack is once again rolling and the High Command has recalled you to the Pacific Fleet. So far we have not been able to make any headway onto the Chinese mainland. You are to land at Poronask under cover of our fleet and rapidly secure the entire island before the Chinese have a chance to use their rockets on the Japanese homeland.

The Russians appear incapable of halting your relentless advance despite their claims of technological superiority. This victory at Ulan Ude proves the worth of our nation’s people, and their most capable leaders.

The Russians are stumbling in their own backyard, and your relentless victories have them more concerned with finding cover than fighting back. With Kazan secure and the Trans-Siberian Railroad feeding out troops steady supplies, the People’s Republic of China is well prepared to hold its gains in the Urals.

The Russians expended great effort and resources to rebuild their forces, and your disastrous loss at Almaty has thrown it all away. The U.S. did not invest its defense budget toward technological superiority for you to stumble blindly into battle like some Viking berserker with a blunt sword. You must drive the enemy into the ocean and seize the island of Singapore securing complete control of the Malay Peninsula.

The crumbling alliance of the Western nations has managed to assemble significant forces on the Malay Peninsula in a last ditch effort to hold on to their imperialist possessions. As the only modern port on the west coast of Malaysia, the capture of Penang is critical to our efforts of strengthening our defenses against the threats from the west. You must advance across the Rai River to seize Penang, and secure the roads south in preparation for an assault on Singapore.

The crumbling alliance of the Western nations has managed to back significant forces on the Malay Peninsula in a last ditch effort to hold on to their imperialist possessions. As the only modern port on the west coast of Malaysia, the capture of Penang is critical in our efforts towards strengthening our defenses against the threats from the west.

The debacle in Burma which resulted from your failure to secure Rangoon has left the People’s Republic of China with insufficient forces to defend its interests in Southeast Asia. The Americans are poised to invade Vietnam. You are responsible for the extreme costs your ill-advised tactics caused and will report directly to the Chinese High Command for an accounting of your actions.

The debacle in Thailand which resulted from your failure to secure Bangkok has left the People’s Republic of China with insufficient forces to defend its interests in Southeast Asia. The Americans are poised to invade Vietnam. You are responsible for the extreme costs your ill-advised tactics caused and will report directly to the Chinese High Command for an accounting of your actions.

The debacle in Thailand which resulted from your failure to secure Bangkok has left the Socialist Republic of Vietnam with insufficient forces to defend its interests in Southeast Asia. U.N. forces are poised to invade Vietnam. You are responsible for the extreme costs your ill-advised tactics caused and will report directly to the Prime Minister to account for of your actions.

The decadent wastes of a corrupted nation are nowhere more evident than the pollution permeating the industrial belt around Kazan. Nevertheless, it is a strategic prize that will serve as a bulwark against the troops stationed in defense of Moscow. You must take Kazan quickly and push the advance west across the Volga River to secure the region.

The decadent wastes of a corrupted nation are nowhere more evident than the pollution permeating the industrial belt around Kazan. You must take Kazan quickly and push the advance west across the Volga River to secure the region.

The dragon is missing a few teeth after your triumphant assault on Hanoi. The Western nations have never appeared stronger than they do with the liberation of Vietnam and the expulsion of China from Southeast Asia that you brought about. It is an accomplishment you can look on with pride, as the chances for long term stability in the region rise to new heights.

The final key to controlling Korea is its port city Pusan at the southern tip of the peninsula. Its capture will signal the reunification of North and South Korea, as well as expell the last vestige of Western influence from the region. The dragon is poised to reveal its unrivaled power and you must complete its rise. Drive all enemy forces from the Korean Peninsula and seize Pusan.

The horde you failed to stop in Kazan is advancing at a breakneck pace towards Moscow. Your defeat has left the Secretary General no option but to abandon all forward operations and prepare for a purely defensive stance.
The key to controlling Korea is its major port, Pusan, at the southern tip of the peninsula. Drive all enemy forces from the Korean Peninsula and seize Pusan.
The key to the Russian Far East is the port of Vladivostok. You must quickly capture the cities along the Trans-Siberian Railroad leading to Vladivostok and secure your eastern flank at Suchan.

The last Chinese toehold in the Russian Far East is at Khabarovsk. Hoping to gain some political advantage, the People's Republic is gathering all available reserves to hold this last section of foreign land. It is imperative that you break this stronghold showing the world that the Dragon has been slain. You must capture the city of Khabarovsk and drive south of the Ussuri River into China.

The loss of Penang is a misfortune of far reaching consequences. Your lack of resolve in serving the People’s Republic of China has revealed your inability to appreciate the need for resourceful leadership. The Chinese High Command has dispatched a replacement for you who better understands the importance of achieving the objectives at hand.

The loss of Penang is a misfortune of far reaching consequences. Your lack of resolve in serving the nation has revealed an inability to provide the need for resourceful leadership. The Prime Minister has dispatched a replacement for you who better understands the importance of achieving the objectives at hand.

The loss of Taejon has allowed the Americans time to land at Pusan, ending any further operations on the Korean Peninsula. You will depart immediately for a personal accounting to the Chinese High Command.

The loss of Ulan Ude put an end to any hope of continuing our advance into Siberia. The Russians are undermining China’s authority with their hollow rhetoric of independence for Mongolia. You are ordered to cease all offensive operations and deploy an occupation force in Mongolia until your replacement arrives.

The magnitude of your loss is immense. The People’s Republic of China has gained the upper hand in the Russian Far East. The threat from expanded Chinese air power on the island has halted the advance on Vladivostok while our reserves must be diverted north to guard the Tartar Strait. It will be some time before we can regroup for another assault. You will be serving stateside when that happens.

The port of George Town (Penang), situated on the western coast of the Malay Peninsula, is critical as a supply line for our shipping which to avoid the dangerous passage across the South China Sea. The retreating People's Liberation Army is, however, laying in wait along the only roads through the rough terrain. You will need to guard against exposing your command to ambush. An attachment of Australian troops are assigned to assist your advance. You must quickly recapture George Town and secure our flank east of the Rai River before the Chinese can relieve their faltering army.

The rebels, who continue to defy all civilized conventions, stand at Ekaterinburg, the gateway to the Urals. The Chinese continue to strip Russia of its precious resources. Your forces must return civilization to this bastion of the barbarous hordes.

The region near Khabarovsk has long been under territorial dispute between the Russians and Chinese. It is imperative that the Russian border is established in no uncertain terms. You must recapture Khabarovsk from the rebels and keep the Chinese forces in their positions south of the Ussuri River.

The retreating army of the People’s Republic of China is laying in wait along the roads to George Town. You must quickly capture George Town (Penang) and secure your flank east of the Rai River before the Chinese can relieve their faltering army.

The so-called liberation of Taiwan by the People’s Republic of China must end. A massive invasion fleet stormed the beaches in the South-West. Expand the landings at Wuchieh, destroy all enemy resistance on the island, and recapture Taipei.
The so-called liberation of Taiwan by the People’s Republic of China must end. Expand the landings at Wuchieh, destroy all enemy resistance on the island, and recapture Taipei.

The taking of Taejon was only a stepping stone, but with it you have won a tremendous advantage over our foes. Greatness, like the unfolding of the thousand petaled lotus, is made of the flawless execution of many small actions.

The triumph of the Government of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on the Malay Peninsula is a victory worthy of our greatest ancestors. With your dramatic expulsion of the Western Imperialists, you have raised a banner of freedom for the people of Southeast Asia. The Prime Minister gratefully acknowledges your most impressive triumph.

The triumph of the People’s Republic of China in reclaiming its traditional territories and restoring its dominance in the Far East hinges on neutralizing our northern menace, Russia. Isolating and capturing Khabarovsk is critical to the success of our expected rise in authority. To that end, you are to cross the Amur River into Russia and take Khabarovsk

The triumph of the People’s Republic of China on the Malay Peninsula is a victory worthy of our greatest ancestors, and the Premier gratefully acknowledges your most capable abilities. With your dramatic expulsion of the Western Imperialists, you have raised an impenetrable wall for the enduring security of our nation.

The vastness of Siberian wilderness makes logistical support the critical factor in our strategy to free Irkutsk and break the stranglehold that the People’s Republic of China has placed on the region. You must capture Irkutsk and Baykal to secure the vital supply lines along the Trans-Siberian Railroad.

The victory you achieved in capturing Khabarovsk has the people of Russia chanting your name in the streets of Moscow. It is curses, though, that you receive from the rebels who relied on their former Chinese ally.

The victory you achieved near Vladivostok has the people of Russia chanting your name. The Chinese High Command, manuvering an army that relies on strength in numbers, simply cannot react swiftly enough to escape the rush of your advance.

The world witnessed a tragic episode in the fight against tyranny when your forces were shattered on the Malay Peninsula. The Chinese are reinforcing their positions throughout Southeast Asia, and with our forces weakened by your defeat at George Town, the chance of any further offensive operations is nonexistent.
This is a victory Commander, another quick blow and this revolution will be over!
Triumph! Your masterful victory at Khabarovsk dealt a mortal blow to the dragon.

Triumph! Your masterful victory at Khabarovsk dealt a mortal blow to the dragon. The People’s Republic of China has sued for peace, offering substantial concessions in order to avoid the embarrassment of an invasion of China, including complete independence for Taiwan. Celebrations erupted the world over as newscasts of the surrendering Chinese army spread. It seems your next tour will be the parade of a hero who liberated a continent.

U.N. indecision to take action in Korea led to a U.S. evacuation of Pusan as the Eastern armies crushed any cities in its path. A month later, the U.S. takes matters into its own hands with an amphibious assault to recapture Pusan.
U.S. forces land in Vietnam and race to capture Ho Chi Minh City in order to secure a northern foothold in Southeast Asia and force the People's Republic of China to withdraw.

Victory is a fortune the bold make for themselves, and yours has earned China great rewards. The Russian Far East is all but secure as the capture of the Trans-Siberian Railroad at Irkutsk will ensure our forces of a reliable supply line.

Vietnam represents an intimidating stronghold for the People’s Republic of China in Southeast Asia and will continue to threaten the security of the Western nations until China’s power there has been neutralized. The liberation of Thailand, however, has left their southern forces in Ho Chi Minh City exposed. There is no better time for our invasion. A U.S. return to Ho Chi Minh City carries with it an importance far greater than the capture of a strategic objective: failure here could spell destruction for the Western alliance. You will begin the invasion at Phu’o’c Tho, then advance north and west to secure the roads and take Ho Chi Minh City.
We counted on you General and you didn't disapoint us. With the Chinese fortified line defeated Volgograd stands open to our attack. Well done!
We have secured a small beachead on the island. You orders are to liberate the island and its inhabitants. Capturing the imperialist den of Taipei is mandatory.

We will strike the Chinese army where they least expect it. As our most experienced and decorated commander, you and your troops have been honored with the assignment to free Southeast Asia. Your goal is the liberation of Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, and the destruction of Chinese armies in Southeast Asia.
Western forces launch a counterattack designed to recapture Bangkok, driving deep into the Chinese held positions in Thailand.

While we were busy in the south, China decided to stab us in the back. They launched a surprise invasion of our country and captured our capitol, Hanoi. This forced us to withdraw from our recent liberated countries and prepare for a counter-offensive against China. As our most gifter commander you are to push Chinese forces back and retake Hanoi.

While you were busy in the south, Chinese forces launched a counter-offensive against our line at Kazan. The Chinese are mobilizing additional forces to protect their hold on it. You must move quickly to retake Kazan before they cross the Urals.
With Eastern forces holding Irkutsk, you must find a way to rout them back to Lake Baikal.

With Mongolia now securely in the protective sphere of the People’s Republic of China, the Chinese High Command has stepped up the timetable for the invasion of middle Siberia. Our first objective is Ulan Ude, a vital industrial center on the Selenga River, which provides an ideal base for our push into Siberia. You must drive up the Selenga River, capture Ulan Ude, and secure the river crossings for the Trans-Siberian Railroad to the west.
With Russia fast crumbling in the war with the People's Republic of China, Japan invades Sakhalin to reclaim the island before China can threaten its northern borders.
With Russia strangling their supply lines to the south, the Chinese forces in Irkutsk rush to dig in as U.S. troops launch an assault on the city.
With the People's Republic of China assembling troops in Khabarovsk to push back the advance of the Western forces, Russia and the U.S. launch a surprise attack across the Amur River.

With the People’s Republic of China reeling from the bloody nose they received at Ho Chi Minh City, our forces are poised to deliver a knock-out blow. After a fiercely contested landing, the port of Hai Phong surrendered. The Chinese, though, are dug in deeply at Hanoi and you will need more than a few well-aimed strikes to dislodge them. Take your forces, drive across the Red River to seize Hanoi, and eliminate any vestige of Chinese presence in the region.

With the Russians having fallen on hard times, the Chinese seeing an opportunity to gain resources have expanded their northern border Kazan. Russia has called for help in restoring order into this wild region.

With the Russians having fallen on hard times, the people of Siberia have revolted. The Chinese, seeing an opportunity to gain resources, have expanded their northern border into Irkutsk and Khabarovsk. Russia has called for help in restoring order into this wild region. The Trans-Siberian Railroad is the critical link in all of our upcoming operations against the Russian rebels and their Chinese allies.

With the Western powers still recovering from their losses in Russia, the Vietnamese are vulnerable to a swift assault down the coast. Completing the conquest of Vietnam should destroy their resistance and solidify our position in Indochina. You must capture Ho Chi Minh City and stop any Western incursions.

With the elimination of the Russian Bear the true objective of Plan Red can now be realized. Fresh from your victory at Volgograd, you have been given the responsibility of seizing Southeast Asia. Your objectives are the elimination of Western influence in Southeast Asia, and ultimately, capture of the vital port of Singapore. This gains the Chinese nation easy access to the newly developed oil fields in the Spratly Islands. The world watches as order is returned to all of Asia under the flag of China.

With your victory at Ekaterinburg, the People’s Republic of China has earned rich rewards. Along with the raw minerals in the region, the massive machine complex at Uralmash and the power plant at Beloyarskoye give China the ability to devote even more resources to military production.
You are to defeat the last remnants of the Thai army and then defeat the imperialists defending Rangoon.
You are to launch a thrust at Almaty near Chinese border in Kazakhstan. Your objectives will be to free Almaty and secure the roads east to Karakamyr.

You are to strike from the port city of Pusan, and take the cities of Masan, Ulsan, and Miryang, as a stepping stone to freeing the South Korean capital of Seoul. What is left of the South Korean Army is there to provide assistance. Good Luck.
You gave the world a bitter pill to swallow with your appalling loss north of Vladivostok. It might be best if you emmigrate to a non-member nation.

You gave the world a bitter pill to swallow with your appalling loss north of Vladivostok. The People’s Republic of China has solidified its defenses in the region and throughout all of Manchuria, making further attempts to recapture the port unlikely any time in the near future. The Joint Chiefs of Staff consider it advisable that you fade into obscurity and have ordered your transfer to records management with the National Archives.
You must avenge a past defeat. It was at Volgograd that a defeated Russian nation sued for peace.

You must avenge a past defeat. It was at Volgograd that a defeated Russian nation sued for peace. It is to be here that we launch the re-conquest of Siberia and the Russian Far East.  A humiliated Russia, ready for vengeance, needs only a spark of hope to rejoin the effort to free Asia.
You must establish a secure area around the city. Push the remaining russian forces and their allies to the Don. This would ensure our domination in Volgograd and will force Russia to capitulate.

Your assault on Ulan Ude effectively clipped the dragon’s wings, leaving the People’s Republic of China incapable of supporting its own weight. No longer will the Chinese be able to plunder Russia’s resources or industrial capabilities to replace their battered equipment. With a few better-aimed attacks, the world will be free of China’s oppression.

Your assault on Ulan Ude has left the People’s Republic of China incapable of supporting the rebels. No longer will the Chinese be able to plunder Russia’s resources or industrial capabilities to replace their battered equipment.
Your command will be split into two groups. One will take Hue. The other one must attack Da Nang. Select your best troops for the offensive and take advantage of the surprise.

Your conquest of the South Korean Peninsula and recapture of Seoul has sent the North Korean diplomats scurrying to sign treaties. Hoping to keep their sovereignty, they have accepted our terms and have withdrawn from active conflict. Excellent job, commander.  You have won an "unwinable" war.

Your conquest of the South Korean Peninsula and recapture of Seoul has sent the North Korean diplomats scurrying to sign treaties. Hoping to keep their sovereignty, they have accepted our terms and have withdrawn from active conflict. In light of North Korea's capitulation, the High Command has decided to switch the focus of our offensive.

Your defeat at Ekaterinburg has not only squandered troops but valuable equipment as well. Without the mineral wealth of the Urals, we can no longer sustain the expenditure of resources that the war demands. It is time you joined the steelworkers in order to replace the assets that you wasted.

Your defeat at Hanoi has gutted our forces and left the door open for the People’s Republic of China to launch a counteroffensive that could sweep away all our hard won gains. The Western forces have already begun their evacuation of Ho Chi Minh City while the British have abandoned their interests in Malaysia. You are relieved of your command.

Your defeat at Irkutsk was a grave miscalculation that the West could ill-afford. The Chinese shifted the bulk of their armies to the north and launched a counterstrike on Novosibirsk that has effectively pocketed the Russian troops that were en route to join your army. With your forces already decimated, there is no way to prevent their slaughter. You have been allowed to surrender what remains of your command to the People’s Republic of China.

Your defeat at Vladivostok is a devastating blow to our efforts. With the port now securely in the hands of the enemy, the Chinese High Command has no alternative but to order a withdrawal from the region, and a termination of your command.

Your defeat at Volgograd is a disaster of unthinkable magnitude, matched only by the mistake of entrusting you with command. Our positions throughout Russia are now threatened with collapse as their idolatrous cries for the defense of ‘Mother Russia’ have inspired fanatic attacks against our forces in the Urals. Many have been successful. You are forthwith relieved of duty.

Your defeat outside Seoul is a disgrace that cannot be atoned for. The Chinese High Command now sees a reunification of the Korean Peninsula as too costly to the stability of our recent gains. All forces have been ordered to withdraw from the conflict, and North Korean diplomats are en route to P’anmunjom to negotiate a treaty.

Your defense of Seoul was excellent!  It is incredibly bad luck that the Eastern flank of the Korean penninsula has collapsed over by Samchok.  The enemy is making a concerted drive on to Chipyong-ni and Wonju right down the center.  I'm ordering you to pull back so that they don't outflank you too.
Your extraordinary victory at Volgograd is a dagger in the heart of "Mother Russia". Russians are in retreat and the city is ours.
Your extraordinary victory at Volgograd is a dagger in the heart of "Mother Russia". The Russian government has sued for peace and opposes us no longer.

Your extraordinary victory at Volgograd is a dagger in the heart of China. For now, the dagger remains in her heart, and China will trouble us a bit less for a little while.  That should give us just a little bit of breathing room!

Your failure at Irkutsk was a mistake that we could ill-afford. The rebels and their Chinese allies will have another year to consolidate their forces and strip the region of valuable resources. The Russian President has asked for your head. You are to be quickly removed from the reach of the Russians.

Your failure to capture Taejon is a defeat from which the U.S. and our allies may well never recover. The People’s Republic of China has all but admitted its plans to conquer the entire Asian continent, and the only option left is a desperate gamble to recapture Seoul.

Your failure to capture Taejon is a defeat from which the U.S. and our allies may well never recover. The People’s Republic of China has all but admitted its plans to conquer the entire Korean penninsula, and the only option left is a desperate stand to the last man defense of Pusan.  The ghosts of the earlier Korean war appear to be with us.

Your failure to retake Ho Chi Minh City has given the Western forces the justification they needed to begin a massive build up in the Southeast Asian theater. They have landed additional forces in Vietnam as well as concentrating men and equipment for an offensive towards Hanoi. Instead of protecting the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, you have exposed our nation to the gravest danger. The Prime Minister has called for your immediate removal from command.

Your failure to secure Khabarovsk is a costly blow to our efforts in the Russian Far East, and has put doubt in the mind of the Premier. If you are to quiet your detractors, you will need to do better in the future.

Your foolhardy maneuvering around Kazan has cost you your command, and may well cost us the whole of Russia. The People’s Republic of China launched several strikes on Moscow and the armies you failed to stop in Kazan are advancing at a breakneck pace. Caught in the midst of redeployment, the Russians are in no position to stop them. Your defeat has left the President no option but to abandon all forward operations and prepare for a purely defensive stance.

Your foolhardy maneuvering around Kazan was a stupendous blunder that has cost you your command, and which may well cost us the whole of Russia. The People’s Republic of China launched several strikes on Moscow and the armies you failed to stop in Kazan are advancing at a breakneck pace. Caught in the midst of redeployment, the Russians are in no position to stop them. Your defeat has left the President no option but to abandon all forward operations and prepare for purely defensive operations.
Your force is charged with the capture of Ekaterinburg and securing the rail lines running east into Siberia.
Your forces must advance south to recapture the cities along the Trans-Siberian Railroad and secure a flanking position at Suchan against Chinese-led forces.

Your humiliating defeat at the hands of the Western forces has plunged Vietnam into a perilous dilemma: risking additional troops defending its positions in Southeast Asia, or surrendering those gains to the degenerate powers of the West. The Prime Minister cannot afford the additional risk of your incompetence. You are hereby relieved.

Your humiliating defeat at the hands of the Western forces has plunged the People’s Republic of China into the perilous dilemma of risking additional troops defending its positions in Indochina or surrendering those gains to the degenerate powers of the West. The Chinese High Command cannot afford the additional risk of your incompetence, and you will be transferred to our reserves in Mongolia.

Your inglorious defeat at Pusan is an end to China’s bid to become the unrivaled power in Asia. The failure to win South Korea has opened the door for a major U.S. presence and weakened our positions throughout Asia. The Chinese High Command must now reconsolidate its forces. You, on the other hand, are to surrender yourself to the South Koreans in order to placate their desire for revenge.

Your loss at Almaty has made a mockery of the People’s Republic of China. Russian troops are streaming across the border into China and now the U.S. has committed its forces as well. The Premier expects you to take responsibility for this failure before you are dismissed from service.

Your loss at Pusan has sent our allies into a panic, as they now doubt the strength of American power. Rumors are even circulating over the advantages of nuclear war. The world has been watching you, and your utter and complete failure could trigger the worst.

Your loss at Pusan has sent our allies into a panic, as they now doubt the strength of American power. Rumors are even circulating over the advantages of nuclear war. The world is watching you, and any future failure could trigger the worst.
Your loss at Seoul was nothing less than the defeat of South Korea itself.  We have nothing left to do but to hang our heads in shame at the negotiating tables.

Your loss at Seoul was nothing less than the defeat of civilization. With no hope of a U.N. victory over the People’s Republic of China, the Russians have launched a limited nuclear strike on the Chinese occupational force in Vladivostok. That it was not on Chinese soil was all that prevented a full-scale nuclear exchange, but that is unlikely to hold. Priests, not commanders, are what the world needs now.

Your loss at Seoul was nothing less was terrible, but HQ hasn't backed you up properly, and the South Koreans weren't as well prepared as we felt they would be.  I want you to fall south until you can stabilize the line further.  We're not going to roll over for the enemy.

Your loss at Volgograd is the worst disaster that I can think of since the Germans lost here during WWII.  But at least at that time, they were the bad guys!  The Russian people want your head, and I'm going to have to give it to them.

Your loss of Ho Chi Minh City has given Western forces the justification they needed to begin a massive build up in the Southeast Asian theater. They have landed additional forces in Vietnam, and have been concentrating men and equipment for a counteroffensive in the north. Instead of protecting the People’s Republic of China, you have exposed our nation to the gravest of dangers. The Premier has called for an immediate termination of your command.

Your masterful triumph is unparalleled and completes the rise of the People’s Republic of China as the undisputed power in Asia. As our newest member in the Chinese High Command, you are to be given control of all occupational forces from the Urals to Pusan. Well done!

Your mission is to recapture the city of Volgograd, destroying all Chinese forces in the area. This city is significant not only for its industrial infrastructure and strategic location, but for what it symbolizes to the world: freedom from Chinese oppression. Again one more critical battle must be fought in its streets. The free nations of the world are watching this battle. Failure is not an option.

Your offensive in Siberia was a success and the High Command has recalled you to the Pacific Fleet. Our new Japanese allies fear long range rocket strikes from the island of Sakhalin and we have tasked you with clearing this island. Intelligence reports that there is a large Chinese army present. You are to land at Poronask under cover of our fleet and rapidly secure the entire island before the Chinese have a chance to use their rockets on the Japanese homeland.

Your smashing the defenses at Kazan has thrown the rebel forces into chaos; and with the supply line now secured, we have the means to press the attack that will prevent the People’s Republic of China from regrouping.
Your spectacular victory at Singapore has decimated the Chinese forces. With our air and naval blockade now firmly in place, reinforcements for their troops in the north are slow in coming.

Your suprise attack near Suchan left the rebels with no hope of stopping our advance. The last remnants of the rebel army are now trying desperately to defend Vladivostok. You are to take the city and defeat the rebels for good.

Your victory at Almaty has exceeded the hopes of even our most optimistic military planners. You have severely weakened the Russians and provided us with a second approach into the Urals. The Premier with excitement and confidence has insisted that you command our operations in the Urals.

Your victory at Astrakhan not only captured a critical strategic objective, it captured the world’s attention as well. Countries are beginning to believe it possible to put an end to the tyranny inflicted on other nations by China and are pledging full assistance instead of empty rhetoric. Even the world press seems captivated by your exploits. They have given you the name "Dragon Slayer."

Your victory at Irkutsk shattered Chinese resistance west of Lake Baikal. The remnants of that army has retreated behind the Mongolian border. This gives our forces the extra time they need to consolidate and bring up reinforcements. There may be no end to the supply of troops for the People's Republic of China, but the ghosts of our defeat here four years ago can now rest as you have avenged them.
Your victory at Irkutsk shattered Chinese resistance west of Lake Baikal. You must continue the push before the snows start falling.

Your victory at Pusan has earned you the thanks from the South Korean President, as well as the respect of our allies. More than securing a base of operations, you have quieted the rumors of nuclear war. The world is watching you, and they are reassured by your display of American military prowess.

Your victory at Pusan has earned you the thanks from the South Korean President, as well as the respect of our allies. More than securing a base of operations, you have quieted the rumors of nuclear war. The world is watching you, and they are reassured by your display of American military prowess.  Now start marshalling forces for the full liberation of South Korea.

Your victory at Rangoon smashed the imperialist holdings in the western Indochina. The new popular Burmanese government sent his best wishes for your liberation of their country. They even comitted their forces to aid us in the liberation of the rest of Indochina, particularly in the Malay Peninsula.

Your victory at Taejon have provided us with the extra time we needed to prepare for a decisive attack to liberate Seoul.  Meanwhile Japan has pledged a significant package of economic support. The Chinese showed the world how well they could march against a weak foe, but now we will see how they are at running backwards.

Your victory at Taejon have provided us with the extra time we needed to prepare for a decisive attack. The North Koreans are pulling back to 38th parallel, while Japan has pledged a significant package of economic support. The Chinese showed the world how well they could march against a weak foe, but now we will see how they are at running backwards.

Your victory at Taejon should have provided us with the extra time we needed to prepare for a decisive attack to liberate Seoul.  But in spite of your excellent defense, the Chinese and the North Koreans keep leap frogging down the eastern flank.  I am ordering you to fall back again.

Your victory at Vladivostok dealt the rebels a mortal blow. Celebrations erupted in Moscow as newscasts of the surrendering rebel army spread. You must return to Moscow immediately; the Russian President wants to personally raise a toast in your honor. You must then go to New York, to receive an ovation before the General Assembly - an ovation you deserve tremendously.

Your victory has once again vindicated the Premier’s confidence in your abilities and the wisdom of helping our allies. We now have the opportunity of eliminating the last foothold of Western power on the Asian coast.

Your victory in Thailand has driven a wedge deep into the cracks among the Western nations. Their fractious and covetous nature has them bickering over the spoils of defeat as they squabble among themselves for false assurances. The Premier is confident that your leadership will soon see a dissolution of Western influence in Southeast Asia and a return to the respectful and orderly values of our people.

Your victory in Thailand has driven a wedge deep into the cracks between the Western nations. Their fractious and covetous nature has them bickering over the dregs of defeat as they squabble among themselves for false assurances. The Prime Minister is confident that your leadership will soon see a dissolution of Western influence in Southeast Asia and a return to the respectful and orderly values of our people.

Your victory near Vladivostok cannot be understated. You have given us a tremendous advantage by securing a base of supply and destroying Russia's Eastern Army. Russia's attempt to mobilize their population has failed and their economy is broken. Siberia lays open to our forces. The Premier is very pleased.

Your victory north of Vladivostok dealt the rebels a mortal blow. Celebrations erupted in Moscow as newscasts of the surrendering rebel army spread. You must return to Moscow immediately; the Russian President wants to personally raise a toast in your honor. You must then go to New York, to receive an ovation before the General Assembly - an ovation you deserve tremendously.

Your victory north of Vladivostok was a complete blow for the rebels. With no hope of holding us, their leaders are preparing for a last stand on Vladivostok, hoping that China will eventually come to their aid. Hope is all they have left.

Your victory over the Vietnamese was complete and the Premier was impressed with the resourcefulness you displayed under difficult circumstances. The capture of Ho Chi Minh City provides us with a firm foundation from which we will be able to dominate any activity in the South China Sea, as well as establishing our undisputed control of the Spratly Islands.

Your victory over the Western powers was complete and the Prime Minister was impressed with the resourcefulness you displayed under such difficult circumstances. The removal of Western-backed governments in Southeast Asia provides us with a firm foundation from which we will be able to end social evils, corruption, and wrongdoing in the region.
